//: Story Phase 5 crew dialogue, one script per crew member per story state (see data/npcs/phase5_crew.json for the selectors), plus what they say about Squawks and their complaints about the Grand Stenchmaster's office.
hale.p5_squawks: hale[concerned]: I've put it in the log, Captain. 'Ship's parrot. Status: bald. Spirits: hostile.' Seemed fairest.
hale.p5_complaint: hale[annoyed]: He's asked for a 'deputy', Captain. To do the parts of the job that involve standing up. Nobody's applied. I've told him the post is permanently vacant.
hale.p5_s9_1: hale: The rule's nailed up, the watch is set, and the Grand Stenchmaster's watching a fish. As days go, Captain, I'd call that a draw.
hale.p5_s9_2: hale[resigned]: Every time that television hums, half the watch looks round. Nobody says anything. Everybody looks.
hale.p5_s8: hale[happy]: One useful thing. I've written it in the log, Captain. Underlined. Twice. The first entry I've underlined since we left port.
hale.p5_s7: hale[alarmed]: Every bell, every rail, every fin in the sea, Captain. All at once!
hale.p5_s6: hale[resigned]: I've seen admirals in full dress, Captain. Kings at their coronations. I've never seen anything like that coat. I hope I never do again. I'll see it tomorrow.
hale.p5_s5: hale[concerned]: Nobody's seen Garrick for an hour, Captain. That's either very good news or the worst news of the year.
hale.p5_s4_1: hale[resigned]: The station's in the log now, Captain. 'Grand Stenchmaster's Office, midships.' I had to. It's there. It's got a chair.
hale.p5_s4_2: hale: The crew have started walking the long way round the station so they don't have to see it. It's added ten minutes to every watch.
hale.p5_s3: hale[annoyed]: I've had admirals with fewer duties than that man, Captain. Mind you, I've had admirals who did less.
hale.p5_s2: hale[concerned]: I've been at sea thirty years, Captain. I've seen men run from cannon fire slower than they ran from that bell.
hale.p5_s1_1: hale[resigned]: Rounds, Captain. Pete at the rail, Gristle in the hold, Jim in the galley, Bob in the crew quarters. Garrick in his chair. That last one's not a round. That's a fixture.
hale.p5_s1_2: hale: The bell's coughed twice since dawn. Neither of them were the Center. Both of them were Garrick sitting down too hard.
quill.p5_complaint: quill[annoyed]: He wants an expense account. For crayons. I've told him we have no money. He said 'then put it on the ACCOUNT'. There's no account! That's what 'no money' means!
quill.p5_s9: quill: For the record, Captain, the Grand Stenchmaster has used his one useful thing for today. I've a tally. It's the shortest tally I keep.
quill.p5_s8: quill[happy]: I wrote it out in my best hand, Captain. I've kept a copy. I've kept three copies. In different places.
quill.p5_s7: quill[alarmed]: I can't write fast enough, Captain! Sharks, Center, wheel, parrot! I've run out of columns!
quill.p5_s6: quill[devastated]: Five medals. I've checked the naval lists, the merchant lists and the honours rolls. He isn't on any of them. He's only on HIS.
quill.p5_s5: quill: The tablecloth inventory is down by one, Captain. The good one. With the anchor.
quill.p5_s4: quill[annoyed]: He's asked me to start a ledger for the S.E.S. 'Viewing hours.' I've refused. On principle. And because the numbers frighten me.
quill.p5_s3: quill[annoyed]: I've itemised it, Captain. Every part in that television. A lantern, a compass, eleven forks, a cannon lock, three bottles, a potato. None of it adds up to a television. I've checked the sum four times.
quill.p5_s2: quill[sad]: I've kept a feather count for Squawks every day since the treasure room. I've just written zero. I didn't like writing zero.
quill.p5_s1: quill[concerned]: I've added a new column to the ledger, Captain. 'Things under sheets.' There's only one entry. It hums.
wick.p5_squawks: wick[sad]: I'll knit him something. I can't knit. I'll learn. Mags can show me.
wick.p5_complaint: wick[disgusted]: He sent his socks to the wash with a note. 'Ceremonial. Do not wring.' I wrung them. I wrung them for a long time.
wick.p5_s9: wick: I've put the shirts through again. Still yellow. But softer. I've decided softer counts.
wick.p5_s8: wick[happy]: He booted a shark, Captain! With the brass boot! I saw it! Nobody believes me and I SAW it!
wick.p5_s7: wick[alarmed]: The quarterdeck! THE QUARTERDECK! The wheel's gone right into it!
wick.p5_s6: wick[surprised]: The stitching's actually very good. I hate that. I'd hoped it'd be terrible.
wick.p5_s5: wick: Somebody's been at the sewing kit. Every needle, gone. Every pin. Jim's tablecloth. I'm not saying who. I don't need to.
wick.p5_s4_1: wick[sad]: My washing. My WASHING. Every shirt on the ship is the colour of mustard now. They crunch.
wick.p5_s4_2: wick: The Frog Grog's gone a bit fizzy today. Mags says it's 'developing'. I don't want it to develop. I want it to stop.
wick.p5_s3: wick[surprised]: A TELEVISION. What's a television? ...And why's it got a potato?
wick.p5_s2: wick[sad]: Poor little beggar. He used to bite me every morning. Never thought I'd miss it.
wick.p5_s1: wick: Washing day, Captain. I've got every shirt on the line. Fresh water's gone, so it's sea water and hope.
fennimore.p5_squawks: fennimore[concerned]: Physically? He's a bald parrot in a sweater. Otherwise? Furious, Captain. I'm prescribing rest, warmth and as many people as possible to be furious at.
fennimore.p5_s9: fennimore: He's asleep. Properly asleep, for the first time in days. Keep your voice down, Captain, or he'll wake up and tell you about it.
fennimore.p5_s8: fennimore[happy]: Squawks asked me to tell you the coat smells. He said it twice, so I think he's feeling better.
fennimore.p5_s7: fennimore[alarmed]: I took him up there for the SUNSET, Captain! It was meant to be the one nice thing today!
fennimore.p5_s6: fennimore[smug]: I've taken his pulse, Captain. He asked me to. In the suit. He wanted a doctor to 'confirm the effect'. His pulse was fine. Mine wasn't.
fennimore.p5_s5: fennimore: If he's hurt himself somewhere, Captain, I'd like to know before the crew find out. They'd want to have a look.
fennimore.p5_s4: fennimore[concerned]: Three men with grog stomach this morning, two with Center cough, one with a splinter the size of a belaying pin. And one man in a chair with a mild case of comfort.
fennimore.p5_s3: fennimore[annoyed]: I've been asked if the television is safe to stand near. I'm a ship's surgeon, not a sorcerer. My professional advice is: no.
fennimore.p5_s2: fennimore[concerned]: He's taken it hard, Captain, but he's eating. If anything, losing the last of it seems to have made him angrier, and angry is good. Angry is alive.
fennimore.p5_s1: fennimore: I've put Squawks out by the mainmast in his basket, Captain. A bit of sun does them good. Doctor's orders. Mine.
rook.p5_squawks: rook[concerned]: I ran right past him. I didn't stop. I'd have stopped. You got there first. I'd have stopped. I keep saying that.
rook.p5_complaint: rook[annoyed]: The noise, Captain. That television. Day and night. Hiss, hiss, turnip, hiss. I dream in static now.
rook.p5_s9: rook: Fair's fair, Captain. He booted one. Right on the nose. I'll give him that. I won't give him anything else, but I'll give him that.
rook.p5_s8: rook[laugh]: 'Providing leadership.' I said NO so loud I heard it come back off the sails.
rook.p5_s7: rook[alarmed]: Captain! Starboard bow, port quarter, everywhere in between! They've brought FRIENDS!
rook.p5_s6: rook[disgusted]: He's started saluting people. Nobody salutes back. He salutes them again, harder.
rook.p5_s5: rook: If he's gone to help, Captain, I'll eat my hat. Well. I'll eat my other hat. I lost the first one running.
rook.p5_s4: rook[annoyed]: He delegated me. To the RUDDER. In the middle of the good bit, apparently. I hope the turnip wins.
rook.p5_s3: rook[annoyed]: Contractual disagreement. CONTRACTUAL. There's no contract! Nobody signed anything! He's never signed anything in his life except his own medals!
rook.p5_s2: rook[alarmed]: I ran so fast I lost a boot. I don't care. I'll grow another one before I grow a bald head.
rook.p5_s1: rook[annoyed]: He's been staring at that sheet since four bells. I asked what's under it. He said 'the future'. I said the future doesn't hum. He said 'it does now'.
sully.p5_squawks: sully[sad]: He looked at me and said 'Drafty.' Just that. I had to go and stand by the rail for a bit.
sully.p5_complaint: sully[annoyed]: He changed the channel in the middle of Shark Duty and shouted 'THE FISH IS BACK!' I nearly went over the rail. I thought he meant a BIG fish.
sully.p5_s9: sully: I'll take a shift tomorrow, Captain. Somebody's got to. And now somebody ELSE has got to, once. I want to be there when he does.
sully.p5_s8: sully[happy]: One useful thing a day! That's one more than he managed yesterday! That's infinite percent, Captain!
sully.p5_s7: sully[alarmed]: Both rails, Captain! They're coming over the BOTH of them!
sully.p5_s6: sully[disgusted]: A suit. A SUIT. While we're up to our knees in shark. I'd laugh if I had the breath.
sully.p5_s5: sully: The starboard side never used to get bitten. They've worked out it's got wood on it too.
sully.p5_s4_1: sully: Mags put a ration of grog out for the rail crew. I drank it. Why do I keep doing that?
sully[queasy]: ...Because it's either that or Frog Water, that's why.
sully.p5_s4_2: sully[annoyed]: 'Excellent shark repulsion!' If he says that one more time I'm going to repulse HIM.
sully.p5_s3: sully[annoyed]: I've been hitting sharks with a mop since breakfast. He's been watching a man and a TURNIP. There's no justice on this ship. There's no justice on this OCEAN.
sully.p5_s2: sully[sad]: The bird. The poor little bird. I've got a nephew that age. Well. Not a parrot. But the same age.
sully.p5_s1: sully[annoyed]: Same patch as yesterday, Captain. Same shark too, I think. He's got a scar shaped like Pete's hammer.
brask.p5_complaint: brask: He told me I wasn't allowed to stand in front of the S.E.S. Then he told me I wasn't allowed to stand BEHIND it. I asked where I'm allowed to stand. He said 'elsewhere'.
brask.p5_s9: brask: Washroom's free, Captain. Finally. I'd still wait a minute. It's still warm.
brask.p5_s8: brask[laugh]: One. He gets to do one. I've seen men in the stocks with better contracts.
brask.p5_s7: brask[alarmed]: I've run out of things to throw at them! I threw a CHAIR! Not his chair. Unfortunately.
brask.p5_s6: brask[surprised]: He's got a door hinge glued to his boot. A DOOR HINGE. I know which door it's off and I want it back.
brask.p5_s5: brask: If he's not helping, Captain, can I shoot HIM? Just a little bit? In the hat?
brask.p5_s4: brask: Still waiting for the washroom. It's been in there an hour. I don't know what it's doing in there and I don't want to.
brask.p5_s3: brask[laugh]: Can I shoot it, Captain? The television? Just once? It looks like it'd make a lovely noise.
brask.p5_s2: brask[alarmed]: Three bells. THREE. I was halfway through shaving. Look at me. Half a man.
brask.p5_s1: brask[laugh]: I've a wager on with Rook, Captain. He says it's a cannon under that sheet. I say it's a still. Either way, I'm getting near it.
gristle.p5_squawks: gristle[concerned]: He'll pull through, Captain. He's too stubborn not to. He told me to stop looking at him. That's a good sign. He's never asked politely in his life.
gristle.p5_complaint: gristle[annoyed]: He's put the station right in the middle of the deck, Captain. Every route anywhere goes past him. You can't get to the rail without being told you're doing excellent work.
gristle.p5_s9: gristle: Night, Captain. Count's done. We're down a tablecloth, a cheese, eleven forks and a compass. And up one television. I've no column for that.
gristle.p5_s8: gristle[smug]: I nailed it up. Twelve nails. Eye level. He'll see it every time he gets up from that chair. So, once a day.
gristle.p5_s7: gristle[alarmed]: All of 'em, Captain! All at once! It's like they planned it!
gristle.p5_s6: gristle[disgusted]: 'Somebody has to establish the standards.' He said it like it was nothing. It's NOT nothing, is it? Who else would there be?
gristle: ...Never mind. I don't want to know. Pass me a hammer.
gristle.p5_s5: gristle[concerned]: He's not helping, Captain. I'll bet the ship he's not helping. Mind you, I've not got much ship left to bet.
gristle.p5_s4: gristle[annoyed]: I've counted his duties, Captain. Nine. I've counted how many of them involve a shark. None. I've counted how many involve sitting. All nine. Even the farting.
gristle.p5_s3: gristle[annoyed]: 'Seat readiness'. I've been ready for that man to sit somewhere else for MONTHS.
gristle.p5_s2_1: gristle[concerned]: He went bald in one go, Captain. ONE go. That's all it took. I'm not ashamed to say I ran faster today than I've run since the Navy.
gristle.p5_s2_2: gristle: Frog Grog, Captain? ...No. Me neither. I've had three. I'd lick the mast first.
gristle[queasy]: Don't, mind. Garrick says the mast's concentrated.
gristle.p5_s1: gristle[annoyed]: Can't finish the count, Captain. Every time I start it, the Center comes and I lose me place.
jory.p5_squawks: jory[determined]: That's what the three bells are for, Captain. That. Him. Nobody else is going like that. Not on my rota.
jory.p5_complaint: jory[annoyed]: He's started calling the duty barrel 'the staff room'. I don't know what a staff room is but I know it's an insult.
jory.p5_s9: jory: Say the word and I'll put you on a shift, Captain. He has to help now. Once.
jory.p5_s8: jory[happy]: I've put him on the rota. 'Emergency: one useful thing. Grand Stenchmaster.' It's the smallest entry on it, but it's ON it.
jory.p5_s7: jory[determined]: Every pole on the ship's in somebody's hand, Captain! Every pole but one!
jory.p5_s6: jory[disgusted]: He made a shark uniform that can't go near sharks. I want that on his headstone.
jory.p5_s5: jory: Starboard's going, Captain. If he IS helping, he's helping somewhere I can't see.
jory.p5_s4: jory[annoyed]: He's started calling Shark Duty 'the front line'. As in, 'how's the front line, Mister Jory?' From his chair. Through a mouthful of biscuit.
jory.p5_s3: jory[annoyed]: Back to work, he says! It's my rota! I MADE the rota! There's no space on it for 'monitoring broadcasts'!
jory.p5_s2: jory[determined]: Good catch with the bird, Captain. If you hadn't got there, I would have. I'd have been slower. I'd have been bald.
jory.p5_s1: jory: Rails are holding, Captain. Holding's the word. Not 'fine'. Not 'safe'. Holding.
bob.p5_squawks: bob[sad]: I said sorry about the grog. He said 'want new crew'. Then he said 'not you'. Then he said 'mostly'. I'll take mostly.
bob.p5_complaint: bob[disgusted]: He's got a bell. A little bell, on his table. He rings it for grog. Nobody brings it. He keeps ringing. It's driving the sharks mad. It's driving ME mad.
bob.p5_s9: bob: Night, Captain. I'm sleeping right here. On the deck. Nobody's moving me. Not the Center, not the sharks, not the television.
bob.p5_s8: bob[laugh]: Odour-retentive! I asked him why you'd WANT that! He's still thinking about it! Look at him! He's still thinking!
bob.p5_s7: bob[alarmed]: I carried four boards and a bucket, Captain! At once! I didn't know I could do that! I can't feel my arms!
bob.p5_s6: bob[sad]: It was not the day, Captain.
bob.p5_s5: bob[happy]: He's gone to help! I can feel it! This is the day, Captain! This is the day it turns round!
bob.p5_s4: bob: I tried his chair while he was out. Don't tell anyone. It's the best chair on the ship. It's the ONLY chair on the ship. Where did he GET a chair?
bob.p5_s3: bob[disgusted]: Why is there a potato. WHY is there a POTATO. Nobody's told me. I can't sleep for thinking about it. Well. I can. But not WELL.
bob.p5_s2: bob[sad]: I offered him Frog Grog. Thought it'd cheer him up. He wants new crew. Can't blame him, really. I'd want new crew if I were him. I'd want new ME.
bob.p5_s1: bob: Zzz... five more minutes, Captain...
ned.p5_complaint: ned[disgusted]: I tried to bring him a shark count. He said reports go through the Stench Log. The Stench Log's covered in DROOL, Captain.
ned.p5_s9: ned: Quiet night. Well. Quiet for the sea. The fins don't sleep. Neither does the television.
ned.p5_s8: ned[smug]: 'Providing leadership.' I said no from the masthead. Loudest I've ever shouted. Felt marvellous.
ned.p5_s7: ned[alarmed]: The wheel's in the poison, Captain! I can't steer by CRAYON!
ned.p5_s6: ned[surprised]: I saw him from the masthead. In the suit. I thought it was a sunset. It was not a sunset.
ned.p5_s5: ned: Can't see him from up top, Captain. And I can see everything from up top. Except, apparently, Garrick.
ned.p5_s4: ned[disgusted]: The long way round. Through the HOLD. With the charts. You should see what the bilge did to the Azores.
ned.p5_s3: ned[disgusted]: Five hundred sharks, Captain. I counted. I'm the lookout. He's the 'Stenchmaster'. Which one of us needed to count, I ask you.
ned.p5_s2: ned[concerned]: Saw it all from up top, Captain. You and the basket and the cloud. Closest thing I've seen since the treasure room.
ned.p5_s1: ned: Fins to port, fins to starboard, fins astern. Fins ahead, too. I think they've worked out where we're going.
nell.p5_complaint: nell[annoyed]: The light off that television shines straight into the binnacle at night. I steered by it for an hour before I realised it wasn't the compass.
nell.p5_s9: nell: Two ribbons on the spoke now, Captain. One for the Center. One for when the first one's been in the Center. It's a system.
nell.p5_s8: nell[happy]: Back on course, Captain. And there's a rule now. I feel better about the rule than the course, if I'm honest.
nell.p5_s7: nell[alarmed]: I've lost the wheel! It's in the poison! We're going round in a circle!
nell.p5_s6: nell[surprised]: I could see the suit from the HELM, Captain. In the dark. It's got a sort of glow.
nell.p5_s5: nell: Steering's fine. Nothing's fine. But steering's fine.
nell.p5_s4: nell[smug]: Admiral's sulking off the port quarter, Captain. He'll be back. They always come back. But he's sulking.
nell.p5_s3: nell[annoyed]: I could hear the whole thing from the helm. 'Executive readiness.' I've been on this wheel nine hours. That's readiness.
nell.p5_s2: nell[concerned]: Is he all right, Captain? Squawks? I couldn't leave the wheel. I wanted to.
nell.p5_s1: nell: Wheel's pulling to port again. Something down there's chewing on the rudder. I've named him already. Don't ask me what.
finch.p5_complaint: finch[sad]: He asked me to climb up and hold the fork aerial 'a bit to the left'. For an hour. I missed my dinner. The picture was a fish.
finch.p5_s9: finch: I'm keeping watch tonight, Captain. If the television shows anything... odd... I'll ring the bell. Once. A small one.
finch.p5_s8: finch[happy]: He did one useful thing! I saw it! I'm going to tell my mum!
finch.p5_s7: finch[alarmed]: They're coming up the anchor chain, Captain! I didn't know sharks could DO that!
finch.p5_s6: finch[happy]: I liked the fanfare. Is that bad? Where did it COME from?
finch.p5_s5: finch: Nobody's seen Garrick, Captain. I looked from the crow's nest. There's no Garrick in the whole sea.
finch.p5_s4: finch: Frog Grog tastes different up the mast. Worse. It's the altitude, Gristle says.
finch.p5_s3: finch[surprised]: I saw the picture from the rigging, Captain! A fish! Going round! How did it get IN there?
finch.p5_s2: finch[sad]: I saw the feathers go, Captain. All three. They went right out over the water. I wanted to catch them.
finch.p5_s1: finch: Ratlines are sticky this morning, Captain. Everything's sticky. I think the air's sticky.
pete.p5_squawks: pete[concerned]: I made him a little hat out of a sock. He said 'no'. Then, when he thought I wasn't looking, he said 'warm'. I'm counting that.
pete.p5_complaint: pete[annoyed]: He asked me to warm his chair while he went for grog. To WARM it. I said I'm on Shark Duty. He said 'that's a no, then', like I was being difficult.
pete.p5_s9: pete[tired]: Night, Captain. I'm going to sleep with me eyes open. In case of bells.
pete.p5_s8: pete[surprised]: He booted it. With the hinge boot. I think I've got to name the patch after him now. I don't WANT to.
pete.p5_s7: pete[alarmed]: REMEMBER THE BIRD! ...I remember the bird. I'm just reminding everyone.
pete.p5_s6: pete[annoyed]: A shark-emergency uniform that can't go near sharks. I've said it out loud four times now and it doesn't get any less stupid.
pete.p5_s5: pete[happy]: I really think he's helping, Captain. I've decided to believe it. It's nicer, believing it.
pete.p5_s4_1: pete[tired]: Not again. That's all I said. Not again. And it was, again. It's always again.
pete.p5_s4_2: pete: Had me grog ration. Then I had Bob's. I don't know why. Something in me wants to suffer.
pete.p5_s3: pete[annoyed]: Grand FIREmaster. I'd be good at it, an' all. I'd set fire to things with RESPONSIBILITY.
pete.p5_s2: pete[concerned]: 'Everything feels drafty.' That's what he said. I've been cold all day thinking about it.
pete.p5_s1_1: pete[tired]: Gerald's holding, Captain. Mostly. I'll do Gerald the Second after lunch.
pete.p5_s1_2: pete: You've got to name the patches. Otherwise it's just wood, and you go mad.
mags.p5_squawks: mags[concerned]: Second sweater's nearly done. It's got a hood, for his head. It's a very small hood. I cried a bit, knitting it.
mags.p5_complaint: mags[angry]: Nine rations, Captain. NINE. He calls it 'tasting'. I call it drinking with a straight face.
mags.p5_s9: mags: Grog's on for the morning, Captain. Somehow worse than today's. It's a gift, really.
mags.p5_s8: mags[happy]: One useful thing. I'm going to hold him to it. I'm going to hold him to it with a ladle.
mags.p5_s7: mags[alarmed]: Everybody grab a pole! Or a ladle! Or anything!
mags.p5_s6: mags[laugh]: I've never seen Jim run that fast. Not even from the Center.
mags.p5_s5: mags: The good tablecloth's gone. The one with the anchor. If he's used it for what I think he's used it for, Jim's going to need holding back.
mags.p5_s4_1: mags: Grog's poured, Captain. One per head. Garrick counts as a head. Garrick counts as nine heads, apparently.
mags.p5_s4_2: mags[annoyed]: The bread, Captain. Jim NAMED the dough. Don't bring it up.
mags.p5_s3: mags[angry]: Grog QUALITY ASSURANCE. He's had nine rations today. NINE. I've a mind to assure HIS quality.
mags.p5_s2: mags[concerned]: I've knitted him a second sweater, Captain. For when the first one's in the wash. It's got a little hood.
mags.p5_s1: mags[annoyed]: The porridge theory was mine, Captain, and I stand by it. In principle. Not in porridge.
jim.p5_squawks: jim[sad]: Soft biscuit soaked in warm milk. No grog. That's what he's having. Doctor's orders. Well. MY orders.
jim.p5_complaint: jim[angry]: He asked for 'a little something' to eat with the television. He wanted it on a TRAY. In his CHAIR. I gave him a biscuit. He sent it back. It was 'too crunchy for the programme'.
jim.p5_s9: jim: Tomorrow's breakfast: porridge. Somewhere safe. I've drawn up a list of somewheres. It's a short list.
jim.p5_s8: jim[happy]: He did a thing, Captain. One thing. I'm going to make him a cake. I'm going to put a bad thing in it, but I'm going to make him a cake.
jim.p5_s7: jim[alarmed]: I've got a ladle and I'm not afraid to use it! On the sharks! Or him! Whoever's nearest!
jim.p5_s6: jim[angry]: Underutilised. UNDERUTILISED. It was for CHRISTMAS.
jim.p5_s5: jim[annoyed]: He went below with me good scissors and a tablecloth. Me GOOD tablecloth. The one I was saving.
jim.p5_s4: jim[sad]: I'd named it, Captain. The dough. I'd named it.
jim.p5_s3: jim[angry]: Different DEPARTMENT. I'll give him a different department. I'll give him the BILGE department.
jim.p5_s2: jim[sad]: I'll do him something soft for his supper, Captain. Squawks, I mean. No grog in it. Not a drop.
jim.p5_s1: jim[angry]: Ask HIM where the Center is, Captain. It's his. It's HIS. It goes where it likes and it likes me KITCHEN.
dunstan.p5_s9: dunstan: Washroom's free. I'm finishing that wash tonight if it kills me. The Center will have to WAIT.
dunstan.p5_s8: dunstan: A rule's a rule, Captain. Even for him. ESPECIALLY for him.
dunstan.p5_s7: dunstan: All hands, Captain! I'm all hands! Both of 'em!
dunstan.p5_s6: dunstan: I'd love a coat like that. Not THAT coat. But a coat.
dunstan.p5_s5: dunstan: Somebody's had all the pins out of the sewing box. I needed a pin. For me towel.
dunstan.p5_s4: dunstan: Don't go in the washroom, Captain. Brask's waiting. The Center's in there. Brask says it was there first.
dunstan.p5_s3: dunstan: I still smell of soap on one side. People keep sniffing me. It's nice, being sniffed for the right reasons.
dunstan.p5_s2: dunstan: Half-washed. That's what I am now. A half-washed man. In a towel. In front of everybody.
dunstan.p5_s1: dunstan: Morning, Captain. Off for me wash. First one in a week. Nothing's going to spoil it.
penhallow.p5_s9: penhallow: Goodnight, Captain. If the television says anything to you, I'd advise not answering. On principle.
penhallow.p5_s8: penhallow[smug]: A labour rule. How modern. In my day we simply threw them overboard.
penhallow.p5_s7: penhallow[terrified]: Is this how it ends? In a COSTUME DRAMA?
penhallow.p5_s6: penhallow[offended]: I have worn a dress coat to a duke's funeral, Captain. That is NOT a dress coat. That is a declaration of war on dress coats.
penhallow.p5_s5: penhallow: He has gone below with linen and shears. I recognise the signs. I was a young man once. With a tailor.
penhallow.p5_s4: penhallow[annoyed]: He asked me to rate the Frog Grog. As a 'man of taste'. I rated it. He didn't like the rating. I've been asked not to rate things any more.
penhallow.p5_s3: penhallow[smug]: A television. Of course it's a television. Why wouldn't a man who invented his own office also invent his own entertainment?
penhallow.p5_s2: penhallow[offended]: That poor creature. In my day we had the decency to lose our feathers to old age.
penhallow.p5_s1: penhallow[disgusted]: I have spent this morning in the presence of a man who believes a bedsheet is a career. I am, as ever, unsurprised.
